claim.quote: The High Resolution Fly's Eye (HiRes) experiment has observed the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin suppression (called the GZK cutoff) with a statistical significance of five standard deviations.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 101101 (2008).

key_value.note: Energy of the observed flux suppression.
key_value.quote: shows a sharp suppression at an energy of $6 \times 10^{19}$ eV

name: First observation of the GZK suppression
notes: AGASA's earlier spectrum (result:agasa-spectrum-beyond-gzk-cutoff-1998) pointed the other way; the HiRes paper itself mentions AGASA's report of events beyond the GZK threshold.

official_url.quote: First Observation of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin Suppression

significance.quote: with a statistical significance of five standard deviations

summary.plain: HiRes saw the flux of the most energetic cosmic rays drop sharply at about 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, where intergalactic radiation is expected to slow protons down. The collaboration quotes a significance of five standard deviations.
summary.technical: Monocular air-fluorescence flux measurements from HiRes-I and HiRes-II show a break (suppression) at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, consistent with the GZK cutoff energy, and the ankle at 4 × 10¹⁸ eV; the Poisson probability of the observed deficit is 7 × 10⁻⁸ (about 5.3 standard deviations), the paper states 5 standard deviations.

title: First Observation of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin Suppression
why_it_matters: The abstract says HiRes measured a sharp suppression of the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray flux at 6 × 10¹⁹ eV, consistent with the expected cutoff energy, and also observed the ankle at 4 × 10¹⁸ eV.
